Hi Sam — great to hear Phase 3 is moving.

Short answers up front: we can do per-project API keys and per-key rate limits; staggered activations are fine. To get this over the line quickly we need:

1) Procurement contact and PO cadence (invoice vs. Net30) — include procurement when ready.
2) Expected monthly token/embedding volumes per app for capacity planning (ballpark numbers are fine).
3) A signed addendum for the additional reserved capacity if you want committed throughput (optional but recommended to avoid throttling during spikes).

I've attached our rollout checklist and a suggested activation cadence (phase3_rollout_timeline.pdf). Logan — quick ask for you: can you comment on KV cache isolation and whether the three apps need entirely separate cache namespaces or can share with project-scoped keys? If separate, we'll provision distinct namespaces.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm procurement PO path and the procurement contact.
- Summit provides rough monthly usage by app (tokens/day or requests/day).
- We provide a short commercial addendum (1–2 pages) showing cost/term options (commit vs on-demand).

Will loop in PrIyom for the commercial draft once we have volumes.

On Thu, Apr 29, 2027 at 10:03 AM kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Logan — quick ask for you: can you comment on KV cache isolation and whether the three apps need entirely separate cache namespaces or can share with project-scoped keys?

Hi all — short tech note:

- For safety and predictable tail latency, we recommend separate KV namespaces per app when apps have distinct traffic patterns (Patient Intake will see bursts tied to clinic hours).
- Per-key rate limits are configurable at the route level; we can apply burst windows and queued requests with graceful 503 fallbacks.
- If you opt into a committed capacity lane, we'll reserve GPU slots and prewarm model kernels for the expected seq lengths (saves ~18% on tail latency).

Action items for Summit devs:
- Provide expected peak RPS and average sequence length per app (or sample prompt sizes).
- Confirm whether data residency requirements require separate deployment regions (we can pin keys to specific regions).

Happy to jump on a short tech sync if helpful — I have availability Mon/Tue next week.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Lead Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — helpful. Sam — following up now that we have the technical picture. Commercial framing:

Option A — Addendum (recommended):
- Commit: +150k tokens/mo across the three apps (pooled) for 12 months
- Unit pricing: committed tier pricing (15% discount vs on-demand)
- Dedicated prewarm for peak windows (optional add-on)

Option B — On-demand:
- Per-key metered pricing, standard on-demand rates, no commit or reserved capacity

If you expect a sustained increase, Option A is the safer path to avoid throttles and ensure latency SLOs. If you'd like, I can prepare a 1-page addendum and an updated quote. PrIyom — can you draft a 1-pager showing the Addendum vs On-demand pricing and include a short note about how the commit impacts support/SLAs?

Finally: please send PO cadence (invoice preference) and cc procurement. Once we have that we'll prepare the DocuSign addendum and schedule keys for staggered activation.

Best,
Kimberly
